w: I work here since three years.
r: I've worked here for three years.
y: Started in the past, still true now: I've worked… for.
a: Since needs a start point. For needs a length of time!
e: I've lived in Lima for five years.
She's worked in sales for two years.
q: I've worked in sales ___ six years.
s: Save this for your next interview.

w: I am interesting in this job.
r: I'm interested in this job.
y: Interested is how you feel. Interesting is the thing.
a: Say I'm interesting and you praise yourself!
s: Send this to a friend with an interview.

w: What I must do every day?
r: What does a typical day look like?
y: In questions, put does before the subject.
a: It also shows real interest in the job!
e: What does a typical week look like?
What does the team do every day?
q: What ___ a typical day look like?
Use does with look like in a question.
s: Save this for the end of an interview.

r: I'm calling about my order.
y: Say the topic first: I'm calling about + thing.
a: Use I'm calling, not I call, for right now!
q: I'm calling ___ an order I received.
Calling about tells them the topic.
s: Save this before your next call.

r: It isn't working properly.
y: For machines, use isn't working.
a: Work here needs -ing, because it's happening now!
s: Share this with someone who fixes things.

r: It depends on the weather.
y: The word after depends is always on.
a: Rely on, count on, depend on. All on!
e: Our plan depends on the weather.
s: Save this. It depends on you!

r: In my opinion, it depends.
y: According to is for others, not for you.
a: According to her, but in my opinion!
e: In my opinion, it's too expensive.
According to the news, it will rain.
m: ME = in my opinion. OTHERS = according to
q: Use in my opinion for your own view.
s: Send this to a friend who debates.

w: How I can send money other account?
r: How do I transfer money to another account?
y: In questions, put do before I.
a: Banks say transfer money!
e: How do I open an account?
I'd like to transfer money to my sister.
q: Questions need do before the subject.
s: Save this before your next bank visit.

r: My bag didn't arrive.
y: Luggage has no plural. Say bags or my luggage.
a: One bag, two bags, some luggage!
e: All my luggage is in one suitcase.
s: Send this to a friend who travels.

w: My bag is too much heavy.
r: My bag is too heavy.
y: Too goes right before the adjective. No much.
a: Too much is for nouns: too much food!
s: Save this before you pack.

r: Excuse me, has the gate changed?
y: For a new change, ask: has it changed?
a: Has + changed shows it just happened!
e: Excuse me, has the flight moved?
q: Use has + changed for a new change.
s: Save this for your next flight.

w: They cancel my flight, give me other.
r: My flight was canceled. Can you rebook me?
y: Use was canceled, then ask: can you rebook me?
a: Rebook is the exact word airline staff use!
e: Can you rebook me on the next flight?
q: It happened already, so use was.
s: Send this to someone who flies a lot.

r: What are my options?
y: Ask for options. The agent will offer solutions.
a: One question opens many doors!
e: I missed my flight. What are my options?
What are my options for tonight?
q: I missed my flight. What ___ my options?
Options is plural, so use are.
s: Save this. Airports can be stressful.

r: So, what brings you here today?
y: Questions put are before you. This sounds friendlier.
a: It sounds curious, not like a guard!
e: So, what brings you here tonight?
s: Send this to a friend going to events.

r: Could you hold on a second?
y: Don't say wait me. Say hold on or wait for me.
a: On the phone, hold on is the normal way!
e: Could you hold on? I'll get him.
q: Hold on means wait on the line.
s: Save this for your next phone call.

r: Let me check and get back to you.
y: Get back to you means you will reply later.
a: After needs an object. Say later instead!
e: Let me check and get back to you.
I'll get back to you tomorrow.
m: LET ME CHECK + GET BACK TO YOU
q: Get back to someone means reply later.
s: Save this for work calls.

w: I will explain you my CV.
r: Let me walk you through my background.
y: Explain needs to: explain it to you.
a: Walk you through means show you step by step!
e: Let me walk you through the plan.
Can you explain it to me?
q: Let me ___ you through my background.
Walk you through is the set phrase.
s: Save this for your next interview.

w: I was responsible of five people.
r: I was responsible for a team of five.
y: Responsible always takes for.
a: Same family: in charge of, but responsible for!
e: Who is responsible for this project?
s: Share this with a job hunter.

r: What are the next steps in the process?
y: In questions, will comes before you.
a: Next steps sounds calm and ready!
s: Save this for the end of interviews.

w: I am very exciting for this offer.
r: I'm really excited about this offer.
y: Excited is how you feel. Then use about.
a: I'm exciting means people get excited by you!
s: Send this to a friend with offers.

r: That sounds fair. I accept the offer.
y: Agree to an offer, or just accept it.
a: Agree with a person, agree to a plan!
e: We agreed to the new price.
m: AGREE TO a plan / ACCEPT an offer
s: Save this for your next job offer.

r: Let's get started. Thanks, everyone, for coming.
y: Say thanks for coming, without your.
a: Coming here is an action, not a thing you own!
e: Thank you for joining us today.
s: Share this with your team.

w: Today we will discuss about the budget.
r: Today we'll discuss the budget.
y: Discuss needs no about. Discuss the plan.
a: But you can talk about it!
s: Save this before your next meeting.

r: Are we all on the same page?
y: Everybody takes a singular verb. This phrase checks agreement.
a: On the same page means we all agree!
e: Are we on the same page about dates?
q: Are we all on the same ___?
On the same page is the set phrase.
s: Send this to your manager.

r: To wrap up, Lee will send the report.
y: To wrap up ends a meeting.
a: Like closing a gift: the end!
e: To wrap up, let's review tasks.
m: TO WRAP UP + who + will + by when
q: To wrap up is used to end a meeting.
s: Save this for meetings you lead.

w: I will present you our app.
r: Today, I'll be talking about our app.
y: Say present to you, or talk about.
a: Present it to you. Always to!
e: I'll be talking about the plan.
m: PRESENT it TO you / TALK ABOUT
q: Today I'll present our app ___ you.
s: Save this for your next talk.

w: My talk is divided in three parts.
r: My talk is divided into three parts.
y: Use divided into, not divided in.
a: Same with split into and cut into!
e: The class is divided into groups.
We split the cake into four.
q: My talk is divided ___ three parts.
Divide into is the correct form.
s: Send this to a friend who presents.

w: Like you see in this slide…
r: As you can see on this slide…
y: Say as you can see, and on a slide.
a: On a slide, like on a page!
e: As you can see, prices fell.
Look at the chart on this slide.
m: AS YOU CAN SEE + ON this slide
q: As you can see ___ this slide…
s: Save this for your next slides.

w: The most important is users want speed.
r: The key point to remember is that users want speed.
y: The most important needs a noun: the most important thing.
a: The key point sounds clear and strong!
e: The most important thing is safety.
q: Add a noun after the most important.
s: Share this with a presenter.

r: Thank you all for listening.
y: Say thank you for listening, without your.
a: For + -ing never needs your!
s: Save this for the end of your talk.

r: So how do you know Emma?
y: Ask with do: how do you know her?
a: This means how did you meet her!
e: We know each other from school.
s: Send this to someone going to a party.

r: I'm really into hiking these days.
y: Like is a verb, so no am. Or say I'm into.
a: I'm into means I really enjoy it!
s: Send this to your hiking friend.

r: No way, me too!
y: Short answer: me too. Not me also.
a: Too goes at the end. Also goes in the middle!
q: The short answer is me too.
s: Tag a friend who says me too.

r: Let's keep in touch!
y: The fixed phrase is keep in touch.
a: You can also say stay in touch!
e: We kept in touch after school.
q: Keep in touch is the fixed phrase.
s: Send this to a friend far away.

r: Are you free this Saturday?
y: Ask if they are free, then give the plan.
a: Want needs to: want to join us!
e: Do you want to join us?
m: ARE YOU FREE + day? / WANT TO
q: Want is followed by to + verb.
s: Send this to a new friend.

w: I will send you message the details.
r: I'll text you the details.
y: Text is also a verb: I'll text you.
a: One short word replaces four!
s: Save this and text a friend.

r: I'd like this fixed by Friday.
y: Use by for the last day. Until means all the time before.
a: Until Friday means keep fixing all week!
e: The shop is open until six.
m: BY = deadline. UNTIL = all the time
s: Save this for your next complaint.

r: I agree with you on that.
y: Agree is a verb. Never say I am agree.
a: Same with I am like. Just: I like!
e: We all agree on the plan.
q: Agree is a verb, so no am.
s: Send this to a friend who agrees.

r: I see it a bit differently.
y: After a verb, use differently, not different.
a: How you see or think needs -ly!
q: Use the -ly word after a verb.
s: Save this for your next debate.

r: Are utilities included in the rent?
y: Use are… included, not is include.
a: Utilities means water, power and gas together!
e: Breakfast is included in the price.
s: Save this before you rent a place.

r: There's something wrong with the heater.
y: Say something's wrong with + the thing.
a: Has problem also needs a: has a problem!
e: There's something wrong with my car.
s: Send this to your landlord. Kidding!

w: I will out of the house June end.
r: I'm moving out at the end of June.
y: Out needs a verb: move out.
a: Move in, then move out!
e: She's moving out at the end of May.
m: MOVE IN / MOVE OUT + AT THE END OF
q: I'm moving out ___ the end of June.
We say at the end of.
s: Save this before you move.

w: How much money I give before?
r: How much is the security deposit?
y: The deposit is money you pay before you move in.
a: You usually get your deposit back when you leave!
q: How much is… asks the price.
s: Save this before you sign a lease.

w: How long is the contract of house?
r: How long is the lease?
y: Renting a home? The contract is a lease.
a: One short word!
m: RENT A HOME = sign a LEASE
q: Lease is the word for a rental contract.
s: Share this with a friend who is renting.

w: You can give more or not?
r: Is there any flexibility on the salary?
y: Start with is there. Or not sounds rude.
a: It opens a real talk!
e: Is there any flexibility on price?
Is there any flexibility on the date?
m: IS THERE ANY FLEXIBILITY ON + thing?
q: Is there any ___ on the salary?
s: Save this for your next offer.

r: Great talk this morning, wasn't it?
y: Short questions need it: wasn't it? Was, because it's past.
a: Was it good? Wasn't it! Match the verb.
m: PAST = WASN'T IT? NOW = ISN'T IT?
q: Use wasn't it for the past.
s: Save this for your next event.

w: I'm afraid that not work for me.
r: I'm afraid that doesn't work for me.
y: After that, use doesn't work. I'm afraid makes a no softer.
a: I'm afraid here means sorry, not scared!
q: I'm afraid that ___ work for me.
s: Send this to someone who can't say no.

w: There is any fees for this?
r: Are there any fees for this?
y: Fees is plural, and questions start with are there.
a: Any goes in questions: are there any?
e: Are there any fees for cards?
s: Save this before you open an account.

r: I'd prefer a refund, if possible.
y: Add a before refund. I'd prefer is firm but polite.
a: I'd prefer is softer than I want!
e: I'd prefer a new one, if possible.
m: I'D PREFER + A + thing, IF POSSIBLE
q: Refund is countable, so use a.
s: Save this for your next return.

w: Let's look the numbers before we decide.
r: Let's look at the numbers before we decide.
y: Look needs at before the thing.
a: Look at, listen to. Small words matter!
e: Let's look at the plan again.
s: Share this with your team.
